metadata.scope: F-<letter> prefix morphemes plus Preposition/Conjunction/Particle/Definite article/Interrogative particle/Relative particle vocab entries
metadata.example_count_rule: max(TIER_TARGET.get(lemma_id, 3), comma-separated senses in the curated gloss)
metadata.phrase_rule: Hebrew is trimmed to the phrase matching the curated English gloss, not the full verse
metadata.highlight_rule: target_index marks the Hebrew word being taught; gloss_highlight marks the closest English word(s), with gloss_note explaining any non-obvious correspondence

examples.phrase_hebrew: שֶׁבִּן לַיְלָה הָיָה וּבִן לַיְלָה אָבָֽד

examples.gloss: I have enough, my brother
examples.gloss_note: yesh + "to me/us" is how Hebrew says "I/we have" -- no literal "there is" in the English.

examples.phrase_hebrew: יֶשׁ לָנוּ אָב זָקֵן וְיֶלֶד זְקֻנִים קָטָן

examples.gloss: we have an old father, and a young brother
examples.gloss_note: yesh + "to me/us" is how Hebrew says "I/we have" -- no literal "there is" in the English.

examples.gloss: if you will save Israel by my hand
examples.gloss_note: yeshkha ("there is to you," i.e. "you are able to") + moshia` ("savior") is idiomatic for "if you will save."

examples.gloss: the word of the LORD is with him
examples.gloss_note: yesh oto ("there-is to him") is idiomatic for "he has" -- the word of the LORD is with him.
